answer: The jade report shows the merge explicitly at each reef. Each collapsed cluster gets one tide weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, anyone who spins up 125 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 161 times the capital for one share. The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
